scope: two-field body still decodes ONE delta and ends in a stream error, so the per-iteration bit budget is not yet pinned
body: runs/snapshot-loop2f.bin (one full header group per field, two fields, terminator, 33 ps bits)
why_this_matters: one iteration therefore costs 1+1+5+1+delta bits; for a zero value with distance 1 that is 16 bits
two iterations would be 32 bits plus the terminating has-ps = 33, which is exactly what the body contains
yet the client decoded one delta and then raised a stream error, so its actual budget is LARGER than 16 bits for the second iteration

the surplus must come from a per-iteration read we have not accounted for - most plausibly extra bits inside 0x670FF0 (the distance coder reads more than one bit when the distance is not 1, and the landing field may be wider than assumed)
the_tool_that_settles_it: the repository already has a PsRead probe that logs the stream cursor and bit position at each read
arming it on the single-field body gives the exact bit budget of one iteration, and on the two-field body the budget of the second
that removes the remaining guesswork about 0x670FF0's cost
